content:
This case concerns the judicial division of a former marital home and garage co-owned equally (50/50) by divorced spouses. The husband sought to dissolve the joint ownership to liquidate his share, while the wife—who lived in the property as the court-appointed custodian of the children—contested the sale, citing the children’s interests and procedural defects in the husband's claim.
A court-appointed expert (CTU) determined that the residential unit was not conveniently divisible into two independent portions without excessive technical costs and significant depreciation. The legal crux of the decision rested on the property's valuation. The wife argued that her right of habitation should lower the property's commercial value for the purpose of the settlement (conguaglio). However, the Court applied the landmark principle of Sezioni Unite 18641/2022: when an indivisible asset is assigned in full ownership to the spouse who already holds the right of habitation, that right is "absorbed" or merged into the full title.
Consequently, the Court ruled that the settlement must be calculated based on the full market value of the property (€183,600) rather than a depreciated rate. The Court assigned the entire property to the wife to preserve the children's living environment but ordered her to pay the husband €91,800 (representing his 50% share) plus statutory interest.
